reasoning_traces.think:
Temporal Conformal Prediction (TCP) extends classical conformal prediction to non-stationary settings by applying a rolling window and correcting coverage errors via Robbins–Monro updates. It avoids distributional assumptions by leveraging exchangeability locally within the window. The core innovation lies in adapting prediction intervals dynamically based on empirical coverage error, using a stochastic approximation scheme. The method’s failure mode occurs when the underlying process violates local exchangeability or when the Robbins–Monro conditions are not met, leading to divergence or instability. In GSI, this translates to adaptive Bayesian inference where uncertainty bounds evolve with data. In GSE, it supports real-time situational awareness by allowing state transitions in response to volatility shifts. The forgetting factor heuristic adds resilience to transient shocks by narrowing intervals after volatility subsides, though it lacks theoretical grounding. This makes TCP robust for forecasting in financial and sports domains where stationarity is violated.
